hero.headline: Martin County deputies capture Fort Pierce man after hours-long swamp search following Palm City hit-and-run
hero.teaser: Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies captured a hit-and-run suspect Wednesday evening after searching for more than two hours through miles of swamp along the Martin County-St.
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies captured a hit-and-run suspect Wednesday evening after searching for more than two hours through miles of swamp along the Martin County-St. Lucie County line. Deputies arrested 39-year-old Likenson Daceus of Fort Pierce just before 6:15 p.m. Wednesday, pulling him from the murky swamp water in handcuffs. Both Daceus and the deputies who tracked him down were drenched from the water after the extended search.

 The incident began with a hit-and-run crash in Palm City near Southwest Rivers End Way. Investigators say Daceus fled the scene and ran through the Windstone community before disappearing into a large swampy area near the county line. His disappearance sparked a large-scale search involving Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies, K-9 teams, aviation units, drone operators, Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission officers, and Port St. Lucie Police Department.

 The search lasted more than two hours as helicopters circled overhead and officers established a perimeter around nearby neighborhoods. The significant law enforcement presence forced the closure of parts of Southwest Murphy Road and temporarily prevented some residents from returning home. The sheriff's office said the coordinated effort ultimately paid off, with technology playing a key role in locating Daceus.

 Court records show Daceus previously had only a handful of traffic-related violations in Indian River County, including driving with a suspended license. Daceus was being booked into the Martin County Jail Wednesday evening. Investigators are continuing to review the case and determine what charges he will ultimately face.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie seeks artists for Botanical Gardens sculptures, photographers for utility box wraps
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie is seeking Florida artists for two temporary Botanical Gardens sculptures and local photographers for a utility box wrap project celebrating the city's natural environment.
cards.body: Port St. Lucie is seeking Florida artists for two temporary Botanical Gardens sculptures and local photographers for a utility box wrap project celebrating the city's natural environment.
